problem: candidate/plugin behavioral relations are themselves stochastic; a deterministic source fingerprint is unsafe

online_negative.method: re-measure chosen source relations online and use majority/mismatch scoring

online_soft_likelihood.method: repeat source relation responses and accumulate smoothed predictive likelihoods rather than hard elimination
online_soft_likelihood.interpretation: soft scoring can trade coverage for observed zero wrong routing, but online remeasurement is expensive and low-coverage

persistent_probabilistic_registry.registration: for each plugin, repeatedly evaluate a fixed pool of 192 relation + 128 bridge experiments and store Bernoulli probabilities
persistent_probabilistic_registry.runtime: candidate sources are not re-run; task observations update posterior likelihood against stored source distributions

active_probabilistic_registry.acquisition: choose the unused registered query with maximum mutual information under current source posterior and stored Bernoulli uncertainty
active_probabilistic_registry.decision: active query acquisition is safe only when source-registration uncertainty is itself sufficiently calibrated; otherwise acquisition can amplify registry estimation noise

current_architecture_implication: a plugin registry should store probabilistic behavioral signatures plus uncertainty and acquisition should account for that uncertainty; runtime source identification can then be active without re-running every candidate plugin
claim_boundary: noise is modeled as iid symmetric relation-bit flips rather than full neural token stochasticity; task observations are noiseless in this source-noise screen; query pool is fixed at registration
next: represent finite-registration uncertainty hierarchically instead of point Bernoulli estimates
test simultaneous task-observation noise and candidate-source stochasticity
validate probabilistic registry using actual stochastic neural decoding rather than injected relation-bit flips
